newsitem.title: USA: Conseco to buy Colonial Penn for $460 million.
newsitem.headline: Conseco to buy Colonial Penn for $460 million.

text.p: Conseco Inc. said Wednesday it agreed to buy Leucadia National Corp.'s Colonial Penn Life Insurance Co. for $460 million in cash and notes, continuing its shopping spree for insurance companies.

The Carmel, Ind.-based financial services holding company also reported $111.5 million in first-quarter profits that slightly exceeded Wall Street analysts' expectations, attributing them to sales and acquistions.

Colonial Penn, probably best known for its television commercials featuring former "Tonight Show" sidekick Ed McMahon, uses direct marketing to sell level-premium whole life insurance designed to meet the needs of seniors with little or no life insurance protection. In addition to television ads, the company uses direct mail and telephone marketing to generate sales.

The transaction is subject to customary terms and conditions, including regulatory approvals, and is expected to be completed in the third quarter of 1997, Conseco said. The company said the transaction is expected to modestly increase operating profits.

Conseco's first quarter net income more than doubled the $46.3 million it earned a year earlier. The company earned 49 cents a share, up from 39 cents a share a year earlier, and revenue grew to $1.099 billion fromn $691.8 million.

The company had record operating earnings of $119.1 million, or 59 cents a share, vs. $48.4 million, or 44 cents a share, a year earlier. Analysts on average had predicted operating earnings of 58 cents a share.
Conseco, one of the fastest growing insurance companies in the United States, has bought at least 16 life insurance companies since 1982.
Its stock rose 62.5 cents to $42 in consolidated late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange. New York-based Leucadia's stock also rose 62.5 cents, hitting $30.25, on the NYSE.
